$comment: THE APP REGISTRY — every deployable thing in this monorepo, declared once.
CI, deploys and provisioning all read this file instead of hard-coding app
names. That is not tidiness: every deployment problem in this repo so far
was a per-app step somebody forgot to duplicate. Tessa's SPA build was
missing from CI, so its whole test suite reported 'no tests' — a PASS-shaped
result — and the merge that added it went red on main. A second provisioning
workflow was copied from the first and drifted. Neither could happen if the
workflows derived the app list rather than repeating it.
`apps-manifest.test.mjs` fails if any directory under apps/ has a
wrangler.jsonc and is not listed here, so a NEW app cannot be forgotten —
which is the actual failure mode, since nobody forgets the app they are
currently working on.
Fields:
id         short name, used in workflow inputs and job names
dir        the worker's directory (holds wrangler.jsonc)
spa        workspace package whose `build` must run BEFORE tests and
deploy — the worker serves it through an `assets` binding, and
Miniflare aborts the suite when the directory is missing.
null for a worker that serves no SPA.
deploy     whether `deploy.yml` ships it
provision  the Cloudflare resources it binds. Omit for an app with none.
email      the display name for its transactional sender. The ADDRESS is
always noreply@4dl.app — one verified sender for the platform,
so a new app inherits a working one instead of a plausible-
looking dead one.
e2e        workspace package running its Playwright suite, or null
`sharedConfig` below is the one resource that is NOT per-app: a single KV
namespace bound with the SAME id into every worker, holding the credentials
the whole platform shares (see packages/core/src/config.ts). Provisioning
creates it once — whichever app runs first — and binds the id it finds into
every app after that. `binding` is the name every worker's Env expects, and
`title` is what the namespace is called on Cloudflare; the workflow matches
it as a SUFFIX, because `wrangler kv namespace create` prefixes the worker
name onto whatever title it is given.
THE PLAYER IS ITS OWN WORKER, and that is the point.
A screen is a DEVICE: one pinned URL, Service-Worker-cached, running for
months without a network. It must not share an origin with the dashboard
— a tenant subdomain would give every studio's screens a different
address, so re-pairing would orphan the cache and custom domains would
multiply certificates by the size of the fleet. It resolves NO tenant
from its host; the tenant arrives from the pairing claim.
`spa` is @scena/player and `deploy` is true, but it binds no D1/R2 of its
own: it is a static PWA plus a proxy to the api worker's sockets.
apps.name: Scena Player

$comment: `preCommands` is how a marketing site gets its `dist`, and without it
this app CANNOT deploy: the deploy job builds `spa` and nothing else,
`spa` is null here (there is no SPA — the generator prewrites HTML),
and `wrangler deploy` then dies on the missing `assets.directory`.
Kova's `www` has carried this line since it shipped; Scena arrived
without it and failed its first deploy on exactly that.
apps.name: Scena marketing
